E1.note: Each inline text node becomes its own line; emphasis is dropped; inline <code> becomes a fenced block.

E2.note: Nested lists are emitted twice: once by extractList recursion and again when the outer walker visits the nested <ul>/<ol>.

E3.note: formatList numbers from 1 and drops the start attribute.

E4.note: Quote markers are not emitted; the quoted text is indistinguishable from body text.

E5.note: extractTable uses cell textContent, so emphasis and links in cells are lost.

E6.note: Emits rows without a delimiter row, so the Markdown is not a valid GFM table. The renderer behaviour on such input is graded unsupported (R6b).

E7.note: Inline <code> becomes a block; the pre>code pair is pushed twice (PRE and CODE).

E8.note: formatEnhancedPageContent emits all prose of a section first, then lists, tables and code, so document order is lost.

E9.note: extractList uses the cloned item textContent, so links and emphasis inside items are lost.

E11.note: Alt text and caption text survive as bracket labels; emphasis in the caption and the image src are lost.

E12.note: The source newline is kept, which is a soft line break in the model-facing text.

E13.note: Quote structure is dropped and the list is emitted separately after the quoted prose.

E14.note: Extraction emits a valid Markdown link with balanced parentheses. Display of the same link is graded separately (R9a).

E15.note: The pre>code pair is emitted twice; the code content itself is preserved.

R1.note:
Each source line becomes its own

; soft line breaks are not joined (solomd2html.js renderMultilineContent).

R2.note: The bare-URL rule runs after link construction and rewrites the generated href; the link breaks and the URL is shown as text.

R3.note: renderListContent fixes the list type from the first line, so a following ordered list becomes items of the first list.

R4.note: CommonMark allows "1)" and "1." delimiters; only "\d+." is detected.

R5.note: normaliseMd splits quote lines and renderBlockquoteContent emits one blockquote per line; a list inside a quote is rendered as literal "- item" text.

R6a.note: Header, alignment and body rows preserved.

R6b.note: Not a valid GFM table. The renderer treats the second row as alignment data; this is a limitation of the supported subset, not a defect claim.

R8.note: Nested strong/em handled; an unclosed "**" stays literal, which is standard behaviour.

R9a.note: Valid CommonMark destination, broken by the link construction plus the bare-URL rule.

R9b.note: Bare-URL autolinking is a local extension, not CommonMark; the link stops at "&" and the remainder is plain text.

R10a.note: Images are outside the supported subset; output is a literal "!" plus a link, not an image.

R10b.note: GFM task lists are outside the supported subset; brackets are shown literally.

R11.note: Setext heading and two-space hard break are valid CommonMark but outside the supported subset.

R12.note: Raw HTML is escaped and shown as preformatted text. This may be an intentional safety choice; no defect is claimed.

R13.note: GFM allows "\|" inside a cell; the split ignores the escape and produces an extra cell.

R14.note: normaliseMd inserts the separating blank lines.

R15.note: The continuation line becomes a paragraph and the following ordered item stops being list content.

R16.note: Backslash escapes are not decoded, so "\*" and "\#" would display with the backslash. Relevant if escaped text reaches the renderer.

E6.reason: adoption rule: gfm emits raw HTML for a header-less table

E13.reason: renderer: blockquote fragmentation and literal list text (R5)
